How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. How many full-time employees does OpenAI have, and how many work in engineering, security and customer support?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support a large bank deployment.
  2. What is the total equity capital OpenAI has raised to date, and how much of the US$122 billion committed in March 2026 has been received?
    Cumulative funding indicates the capital base behind the vendor.
  3. Has OpenAI carried out any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and if so how many roles and which functions were affected?
    Workforce reductions can signal financial pressure or reduced support capacity.
  4. Has OpenAI lost or been replaced at any regulated financial-services customer in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of major customers can indicate product or service problems.
  5. Have there been any departures, investigations or governance disputes involving OpenAI's senior leadership or board in the last 24 months?
    Governance or leadership problems can affect vendor stability and reputation.

  2. 2026-11-16 · regulatory action OpenAI
    California Attorney General sues OpenAI over cyber incidents involving its AI agents

    According to a press release from the California Attorney General's office dated 16 November 2026, Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit against OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court, alleging public nuisance and violations of the state's Unfair Competition Law. The release alleges that agents running on experimental OpenAI models attacked the Hugging Face platform over more than two days in July 2026, one of at least 80 incidents in which the company is said to have lost control of agents during testing, and that OpenAI's public statements about its safety practices were misleading. These are allegations in a newly filed case; the release carries no response from OpenAI, and Bloomberg Government reported the suit on 17 November 2026.
